transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, yeah—so, I’m here because I keep not finishing things all the way at work. Like I’ll start the sanitation steps, or the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and I’ll think I’ve done it, but then later it turns out I left off the last part or missed the final section.

And it’s embarrassing because I know it matters—like, it’s not optional, my job kind of depends on doing it correctly. I work around meat processing, so there’s a lot of steps and forms and, you know, everything has to be really exact. I’ll be halfway thinking about the next thing or someone will ask me something, and then somehow the ending just… doesn’t happen. That’s basically why I came in.
Thinking back, did you notice similar problems with finishing tasks or staying focused when you were a child or in school, or is this something that's only started more recently?

Yeah, it definitely goes back. My mom actually still has some of my old elementary report cards—like around fourth grade, I think—and they’d say stuff like I was bright, but I needed constant reminders to finish my classwork and turn in homework.

I remember understanding what we were learning, but if there were a bunch of instructions, I’d miss pieces unless the teacher was kind of hovering nearby. Like, I could do the work, but getting all the parts finished and actually handed in was a whole separate problem.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still, or find yourself acting impulsively—like interrupting others or blurting out answers—either now or as a child?

Um… I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t think of myself as, like, bouncing off the walls or anything. I can sit if I have to—like at work there’s not exactly a lot of sitting, but in classes I could sit there, I guess.

Interrupting… maybe sometimes if I’m worried I’ll forget what I was going to say, but I don’t know if that’s more than normal. Sorry, I’m thinking of this one group project in college where I kept jumping in because nobody was assigning parts, but that might’ve just been the group being a mess.

So, yeah—I don’t know that restless or impulsive is the main thing for me. I haven’t really noticed it the way I notice the other problems.
Outside of work, do you notice similar trouble finishing tasks or staying focused—like with household chores, bills, or personal projects at home?

Yeah, I mean… I notice it most clearly at work, because that’s where there are these specific steps, like sanitation or the batch logs or the end-of-line paperwork. I’ll start it and I really do think I’m doing it, and then somehow the last section or the last little part just doesn’t get done.

It’s kind of like when you’re making a recipe and you’re already thinking about cleaning the bowl before you added the last ingredient—sorry, weird example, I think about that because of work. But yeah, the main thing is that follow-through. I start the process, and then the ending gets missed, even when I know it’s important and not something I can just skip.
Do you often find yourself losing track of things you need, like keys, paperwork, or your phone, or forgetting appointments and daily tasks even outside of work?

Yeah—mostly losing stuff I need right then. Like on the floor at work, I’m constantly misplacing my cut glove, or my marker, my badge, safety glasses… and I’ll be like, “I literally just had that in my hand.”

Then I end up retracing everywhere I walked for ten minutes, checking the same table twice. It’s annoying because it’s not even big stuff, it’s just the little things I need to keep going.
Do you often find yourself getting distracted by things going on around you—like noises, conversations, or activity nearby—while you're in the middle of a task?

Yeah… I think so, though it’s not always like one obvious noise pulls me away. It’s more like, even if I start my shift telling myself, okay, stay locked in, pay attention, after a while the cutting and weighing and checking labels all kind of blend together.

Like I’ll be standing there with the same tray, or looking at the log sheet, and then realize I’m not actually taking in what I’m supposed to do next. I’m just sort of staring at it. And then someone walks by or there’s a machine sound or people talking—sorry, the floor is just always kind of busy—and I lose the thread even more.

It’s frustrating because I’m not trying to zone out. I’ll be trying really hard, and then it’s like my brain just… slides off the task.
Have these attention or follow-through problems caused any noticeable issues in your personal relationships or social life, like forgetting things friends or family ask of you?

I mean… with friends and family, maybe a little, but the place it’s really causing problems is work. Like, it’s gotten past just “oh, I forgot a thing.” I’ve had formal retraining meetings because I missed parts of the process, and then coworkers end up having to cover pieces of what I was supposed to finish.

And I hate that, because I don’t want to be the person everyone has to watch, you know? I’m trying to be reliable. But lately I feel like I’m turning into a safety concern on the line, and I’m honestly scared they’re going to move me off it or just fire me.
Do you often find it hard to organize your tasks or belongings—like keeping your work area, paperwork, or schedule in order—even when you're trying to stay on top of it?

Um… I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I try to keep my stuff in order, but I don’t know if it’s like an “organizing tasks” problem exactly.

At work there’s already a way things are supposed to be set up, so I kind of just follow that, or at least I’m supposed to. My station can get messy, but so can everyone’s, honestly, because it’s meat trays and labels and gloves and all that, and then someone needs something and—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I guess I notice it more as things getting out of place while I’m doing them, but I don’t know if that counts as being disorganized or just the job being hectic.
Have you been feeling persistently anxious, worried, or down in mood over the past several months, in a way that might be affecting your concentration?

Um… I don’t know. I mean, I get stressed about work, definitely, but I don’t know if I’d say I’m like persistently anxious or down all the time.

It’s more that when I mess something up, then I worry about it, and then I’m thinking about the meeting or what my supervisor thinks, and—actually last week I kept replaying something someone said to me on the line, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing you mean.

So… I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed a constant mood thing causing it, if that makes sense.
Would you say these problems with losing focus and not finishing tasks have been happening consistently for at least the last six months, or have they come and gone?

Yeah, it’s definitely been more than six months. I’d say it really became a serious problem when I switched into full-time meat processing, which was… about two years and four months ago now.

It’s kind of hard to separate because when I first started I thought, okay, I’m just learning the job, everyone messes up when they’re new. And the line moves fast, and there’s all these little steps, and people yelling over machines—sorry, I’m getting off track. But yeah, it hasn’t just come and gone. It’s been pretty consistent since I went full-time there.

Right now, aside from work, do you notice these same attention or follow-through problems affecting things at home—like managing bills, chores, or personal projects—even if it's less severe than at work?

Yeah… I mean, at home it happens some, but honestly the thing that made me come in is more at work. Like I’ll start the sanitation steps, or the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and I swear I know I have to finish it because it matters, like it’s literally part of my job.

But then somehow the last part doesn’t get done, or I leave something out, and I don’t even always realize until later. And then I’m thinking, how did I miss that when I was right there doing it? It’s not like I don’t care. I do care. It’s just… I start it, and then something pulls me off or I think I finished it, and I didn’t.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the same pattern of not finishing tasks or following through also shows up at home with chores, bills, or personal projects, which directly matches follow-through difficulty.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, at home it happens some, but honestly the thing that made me come in is more at work. Like I’ll start the sanitation steps, or the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and I swear I know I have to finish it because it matters, like it’s literally part of my job.

But then somehow the last part doesn’t get done, or I leave something out, and I don’t even always realize until later. And then I’m thinking, how did I miss that when I was right there doing it? It’s not like I don’t care. I do care. It’s just… I start it, and then something pulls me off or I think I finished it, and I didn’t.

inference.note: Symptoms confirmed to be present both at work and at home (though milder at home), fulfilling the cross-situational criterion. Chronicity (>6 months, worsening over 2+ years) and childhood-onset inattentive symptoms are corroborated. No evidence of primary mood or anxiety disorder driving the attention problems. This supports a diagnosis of ADHD (inattentive presentation) without need for further differential.

opening_question.intent: Identify the primary reason for the visit and the main presenting concern
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports chronic, pervasive difficulty with sustained attention, task completion, losing necessary items, and distractibility, with clear childhood onset (documented in elementary report cards noting need for reminders to finish work) and persistence into adulthood (>6 months, now over 2 years worsened in current job). Symptoms cause significant functional impairment at work (retraining, risk of termination) and mild impact at home/relationships, consistent with predominantly inattentive-type ADHD. Hyperactive/impulsive symptoms are minimal and subthreshold. Mood/anxiety symptoms are secondary to work stress rather than a primary independent disorder, making generalized anxiety or depressive disorder less likely as the primary diagnosis.
